headline: Senegal gets its AFCON crown back at the sports court, Germany's president courts investors in Accra, and AI stocks slide again as the Nvidia rebound fades.

items.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills two, wounds 40
items.summary: An overnight Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed two people and injured 40, four of them children, according to the regional governor. Latvia's president said the war could reach a tipping point next year and argued Moscow is not serious about ending it.

items.title: NATO says it will defend against threats in space
items.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance will respond to space threats after reports that Russia is preparing a nuclear-armed satellite. The Kremlin dismissed the reports as hardly worth taking seriously.
items.videoQuery: Rutte NATO space threat Russia nuclear satellite

items.title: Sudan: drones behind most civilian deaths this year, UN says
items.summary: The UN human rights office counted at least 2,230 civilians killed in Sudan between January and October 2026, most of them in drone strikes and the majority in Kordofan. Sudan accuses Ethiopia of letting drones launch from its territory; Ethiopia denies backing the RSF.
items.videoQuery: Sudan drone strikes civilians UN report

items.title: Bangladesh's Hasina says she will return on 16 December
items.summary: A spokesperson for former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia, said she plans to fly home on 16 December. Bangladesh's foreign minister responded that she would be brought back in handcuffs.

items.title: COP31 ends as the longest COP on record, with no cover deal
items.summary: The Antalya talks closed about 50 hours late on 22 November without agreement on the 'Antalya pact' cover text, which the EU and UK rejected for not mentioning fossil fuels. Ghana said it could have supported it. Technical decisions on just transition, adaptation, finance and carbon markets were still adopted.
items.why: Ghana's own negotiating stance is on the record: useful context for your Article 6 research.

items.title: Watchdog: Article 6 rules survived COP31, but 2028 review is the next fight
items.summary: Carbon Market Watch says the carbon-market rulebook came through intact despite heavy industry lobbying, but warns the scheduled 2028 review could loosen it. A market-side analysis by ClimateTrade confirms the 6.2, 6.4 and 6.8 guidance was adopted and the 2028 review stays in place.
items.why: The rules your cookstove-oven credits would trade under are stable for now; watch who pushes to change them before 2028.

items.title: Governments still split on the timing of the next IPCC report
items.summary: Countries again failed to agree a timeline for the IPCC's seventh assessment: most want it ready for the 2028 global stocktake, while a smaller group including India, Saudi Arabia, Russia and Kenya argue for more time. The IPCC session resumes online on 1–3 December.

items.title: Scientists urge WHO to treat El Niño as a health emergency
items.summary: Two researchers called on the World Health Organization to declare this year's El Niño a public-health emergency, citing risks from heat, drought and disease. Carbon Brief also flagged a UNESCO finding that AI chatbots can drop climate facts when users push back.
items.why: El Niño can shift West African rainfall and fish catches.

items.title: Germany's Steinmeier opens German-African Business Summit in Accra
items.summary: President Steinmeier met President Mahama on 24 November, called Ghana a beacon of stability for investors, and said Ghana–Germany trade grew about 20% in 2025. Mahama asked German firms to invest in local processing of raw materials under the New Economy Programme.
items.why: German climate and development funders are in town: a networking window for Carbon Clarity and Yamale.
items.videoQuery: Steinmeier Accra German African Business Summit

items.title: Sports court gives Senegal back the 2025 AFCON title
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld Senegal's appeal, reversing CAF's March decision that had handed Morocco the title after Senegal's walk-off during the final. Senegal had won that final 1-0; reports say Morocco may contest the ruling.

items.title: Cedi down 10.6% against the dollar this year, BoG data show
items.summary: Bank of Ghana figures put the cedi's 2026 depreciation at 10.6% by November, up from 9.5% in September. Fitch Solutions expects it to average about GH¢12.40 per dollar in 2027.
items.why: Credits are sold in dollars and euros: a weaker cedi raises their local value but also the cost of imported sensors.

items.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak still out of control after six months
items.summary: Government data show more than 11,000 cases with nearly half of those infected dead, and Africa CDC says most new cases come from outside known contact lists. MSF says money pledged is not reaching frontline workers.
items.videoQuery: DR Congo Ebola outbreak Africa CDC

items.title: AI stocks slide again as Nvidia's rally fades
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell about 1.5% and Nvidia about 5.9% a day after its surge on Jensen Huang's return, while the Dow rose. Asian markets dropped sharply on Wednesday amid reports Washington is preparing findings that could lead to new tariffs on 16 trading partners.
items.videoQuery: stock market AI selloff Nvidia November 2026

items.title: Anthropic shares slip below their IPO price
items.summary: Anthropic fell 6.5% on Tuesday to below its $83 Nasdaq listing price, part of a wider sell-off in AI stocks. US consumer confidence, meanwhile, hit its highest level in nearly two years.

items.title: IEA: Africa's solar boom is going small-scale
items.summary: The IEA says most of Africa's solar growth now comes from rooftop and small systems rather than big plants: the continent imported about 26 GW of panels in 2025 while only about 10 GW of installations were reported. Nigeria, Algeria, Kenya and Senegal each added over 1 GW last year.
items.why: Small solar for productive use is a growing market next to clean-heat ovens.
items.videoQuery: IEA Africa solar boom small scale

items.title: Leukaemia can start growing 50 years before diagnosis
items.summary: Using stored yearly blood samples, UCL and Cambridge scientists found that in two-thirds of acute myeloid leukaemia cases the first cancer-driving mutation appeared before age 20. Spotting a single dominant blood clone years ahead could one day help predict and prevent the disease.

items.title: Species down to their last 50 animals can recover, with help
items.summary: A study of 141 birds and mammals found 61% of near-lost species that got direct conservation help reached 100 animals, against 2% of those left alone, where extinction was far more common. Removing threats like rats alongside breeding worked best.

good.title: Angola starts building a 90 MW solar plant with batteries
good.summary: Construction began in Cabinda on a 90 MWp solar plant with 25 MWh of storage, built by Egypt's Elsewedy, to serve more than 180,000 people.

good.title: Tunisia gets its first utility-scale battery
good.summary: EBRD and the Clean Technology Fund put €50m into Tunisia's first grid battery (10 MW/20 MWh), alongside a 50 MW solar plant in Tataouine.

good.title: Sierra Leone cuts maternal deaths
good.summary: A national campaign has reached over 10,000 children who had never been vaccinated, and Gavi reports maternal deaths down 32%.

good.title: A rescued bird's big comeback
good.summary: The Lord Howe woodhen, down to 23 birds in the 1970s, reached 1,638 by 2024 after rats were cleared from its island.

good.title: Wild oysters bred again off Scotland
good.summary: Conservationists bred native oysters at a Scottish site where they had been locally extinct for over a century, a UK first.

quiz.q: Which body restored Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions?
quiz.why: CAS upheld Senegal's appeal on 24 November, reversing CAF's March decision.

quiz.q: By how much had the cedi depreciated against the dollar by November 2026, per BoG data?
quiz.why: BoG data show 10.6%, up from 9.5% in September.

quiz.q: In UCL/Cambridge research, in two-thirds of AML cases the first driver mutation appeared before what age?
quiz.why: That is more than 50 years before the typical diagnosis.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.
